title: How exposure management can help public sector prepare for PHP2Shell-like vulnerabilities
description: PHP2Shell refers to two critical memory management vulnerabilities in the PHP runtime (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) disclosed in October 2026. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution on affected web servers. The vulnerabilities were rapidly exploited in the wild within days of disclosure, prompting emergency patches and urgent remediation directives from agencies like CISA. The PHP runtime vulnerabilities pose a challenge because even secure application code can be exposed if the underlying PHP runtime is vulnerable. Emergency patches were released for PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, with further updates addressing additional critical flaws. Public sector agencies were urged to patch immediately or take systems offline to prevent exploitation. The rapid exploitation and widespread exposure (over 30 million PHP services affected) highlight the criticality of runtime-level vulnerabilities and the need for effective exposure management.
